extracted.intended_audience: USPTO Technology Center 3600 (Business Methods) patent examiners, SPEs, trainers, and quality assurance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and internal standards for improving patent examination quality in USPTO Technology Center 3600 (Business Methods), focusing on examiner training, workgroup action plans, quality enhancement meetings, and subject-matter-eligibility (35 U.S.C. 101) instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Quality (overall goal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our goal is to promote and support the continuous improvement of patent products, processes and services through collaboration with internal and external stakeholders of the intellectual property community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize continual improvement across products, processes, and services and engage both internal and external stakeholders in the intellectual property community to achieve improved patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Training Allocation (FY2017: 25 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Examiner is allotted up to 25 hours in FY 2017 to attend elective training that falls within the categories below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure examiners use allotted elective training hours for professional development in approved categories; track utilization against the 25-hour allotment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved Training Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Elective training must fall within: Legal, Policy and Procedure Training; Technical Training; Leadership Training; TC-Specific Legal/Policy/Procedural Training based on TC-Specific Needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select training that balances legal, policy, technical, and leadership development; include TC-specific trainings where applicable to address local needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Balance Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in these categories supports both individual employee development as well as the needs of the agency and provides a balance of legal, policy, technical, and leadership training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and approve training plans that simultaneously meet examiner development goals and agency operational needs; avoid over-emphasis on a single category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corps-wide Training Topics (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recent topics include FY17 Interview Practice Training; Legal Analysis and Writing Part I: Understanding Case Law and the Federal Court System; Legal Analysis and Writing Part II: How to Evaluate and Analyze Legal Arguments Based on Case Law. Upcoming topics include 35 U.S.C. 112(f) and 35 U.S.C. 101 Refreshers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these topics as model curricula for corps-wide skill improvement, particularly legal analysis/writing and subject-matter-eligibility refreshers relevant to exam quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Availability of Training Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All corps-wide examiner training is publically available (https://www.uspto.gov/learning-and-resources/examiner-training-materials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage publicly posted training materials for preparation and reference; ensure trainees know where to access course content and memoranda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Action Plans (workgroup/art unit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each workgroup / art unit prepares a tailored training action plan for their area. These action plans are developed based on workgroup / art unit quality metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create action plans informed by measurable quality metrics at the workgroup/art-unit level; tailor content to local weaknesses and needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous Revision of Action Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers revise their action plans as part of a continual quality focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate periodic review and revision cycles for action plans; respond to identified trends and examination outcomes to update training priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPE-driven Theme Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the review of their particular quality action plan, and individual examiner work product, SPEs identify a number of themes which are addressed through quality enhancements meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPEs should analyze individual and unit work products to surface recurring issues/themes and feed those into targeted quality enhancement sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Enhancement Meetings — structure and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: SPEs empower senior examiners and TC trainers to organize and execute quality enhancement meetings. All examiners are authorized to attend these informal discussions. These discussions are delivered to relatively small groups within Business Methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep sessions informal and small-group to promote interaction; empower senior staff to lead; encourage broad examiner attendance for dissemination of best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 101 Quality Enhancement Meetings — memorandum discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Within workgroups, trainers lead discussions of Memoranda on recent subject matter eligibility, including memoranda on decisions such as Enfish, TLI, Rapid Litigation Management v. CellzDirect, and Sequenom v. Ariosa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use memoranda on recent subject-matter-eligibility decisions as core discussion material; review and analyze memoranda to ground eligibility determinations in precedent and PTO guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Circuit Case Law Deep Dives
rubrics_metrics.description: Within workgroups, trainers lead discussions of various Federal Circuit decisions (e.g., Electric Power Group v. Alstom, McRo v. Bandai, FairWarning v. Iatric, Amdocs v. Openet, Trading Technologies v. CQG, Ameranth v. Apple). These discussions comprise a deep dive look at the claims in question, a summarization and analysis of the decision rendered, and how these decisions can support an eligibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform claim-level analysis, summarize holdings, and explicitly connect case outcomes to eligibility reasoning used in examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on Eligibility Steps 2A and 2B
rubrics_metrics.description: Within workgroups, trainers discuss guidance concerning eligibility in Step 2A and in Step 2B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit instruction on applying the two-step framework (Step 2A/2B) in eligibility analyses; use examples and case law to illustrate application and pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigating the USPTO 'Case Law Chart' and 'Index of Examples'
rubrics_metrics.description: Within workgroups, trainers provide guidance on how to navigate the 'Case Law Chart' and 'index of Examples' located on the USPTO Website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train examiners on how to use USPTO reference tools effectively to find relevant precedent and illustrative examples that support consistent eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business Methods Art Unit Immersion (review cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review 2-3 cases per examiner for an entire art unit. Take the findings and determine if there are training issues which are needed for an entire art unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use immersion reviews to detect unit-level training needs, systemic issues with Office Actions, or patterns indicating outlier performance; document findings to inform action plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art Unit Immersion Goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Goals: To improve quality of Office Action in TC 3600; To evaluate patent examination related issues on an art unit level; To help individual examiners meet goals; Identify Outlier art units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus immersion activities on measurable improvements in Office Action quality, targeted remediation for examiners, and detection of outlier art-unit performance requiring corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Training Time for 35 U.S.C. 101 Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Business Methods area, additional training time has been provided to allow examiners to learn and apply methods from the 35 U.S.C. 101 resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate extra training resources/time to ensure examiners can internalize 35 U.S.C. 101 methodologies and apply them consistently in examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected Examiner Competencies from 101 Training
rubrics_metrics.description: The intention is to allow examiners to: Effectively respond to written applicant arguments; Effectively respond to applicant arguments during interviews; Discuss additional 35 U.S.C. 101 guidance from a SPE and/or QAS; Apply the training materials from prior training and documents; Review the specification for statutory subject matter and document/call applicant with suggestions if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train examiners to (1) craft legally and factually grounded responses to applicant arguments in writing and orally, (2) consult SPE/QAS for guidance, (3) apply prior training materials, and (4) proactively review specifications and suggest possible amendments or clarifications to applicants when statutory subject matter issues arise.
